observation.visible_scene: A silver mesh-grille microphone stands upright in the center of a cylindrical vessel made of densely packed magnetic spheres, against a white draped cloth backdrop. Two hands enter from the top corners, each holding a vertical chain of magnetic spheres that hangs down to the rim of the vessel on the left and right sides.
visible_changes: At the start both chains are held high and taut, running nearly straight down from the hands to the vessel's rim.
The left hand progressively lowers from t=0 to about t=0.6, letting the left chain lose tension and curve/droop onto the left side of the rim.
The right hand then lowers from about t=0.6 to t=1.0, so the right chain likewise bends and drapes over the right rim.

From t=1.0 to t=2.4 both hands continue moving downward and inward toward the vessel, the two chains deforming from straight lines into curved strands lying along the outer walls of the sphere-built container.
Near t=2.4-2.6 the hands open and withdraw toward the frame edges (appearing blurred in the last frames), the chains settling draped over the top rim and down the sides.
The microphone, the spherical container, and the cloth background stay fixed throughout; no camera pan or zoom is evident.
outside_clip_unknowns: The configuration of the chains and hands before t=0 (the holding pose is already in progress at the first frame).
The final resting state of the chains after the hands leave the frame.
The intent behind lowering the chains and whether they are attached to the container or merely resting on it.
uncertain_details: Exact frame of release is hard to pin down as the hands blur while withdrawing.
Whether the slight apparent shift in framing is camera motion or just the hands moving out of view is not clearly supported.
The chains' shape change is a deformation (bending of a flexible strand), not a translation of a rigid object.
